permissions.$denyComment: The pip denies target the BASE interpreter only, which is pinned at exactly 7 packages and must never be extended. Installing into an isolated venv by its full path -- e.g. training/.venv/bin/pip install X -- does not match these patterns and is allowed, which is the intended behaviour for the LoRA work.

$comment: Semi-supervised mode for the SyMoNeuRaL build: file edits and writes apply without a prompt, Bash and everything else still asks. Project-level settings take precedence over ~/.claude/settings.json, which defaults to 'plan' -- that default would stall a fresh agent on its first tool call. This was 'bypassPermissions' for the unattended overnight runs (HANDOVER.md, section 'Running unattended'); put that back only for a run nobody is watching, because it also stops the deny list below from ever surfacing a prompt. For fully supervised work, delete this file or set defaultMode to 'plan'.
$pathComment: Deny patterns are relative globs on purpose. They used to hardcode /home/google/MIT_AI_Training/MIT_AI_Training, which silently stopped guarding anything the moment the checkout moved -- the guard would have been absent exactly when it mattered.
